lA NO: 1 OF 2025  Petition under Section 151 CPC is filed praying that in the circumstances stated in the grounds filed in support of the petition, the High Court may be pleased to direct the respondents herein not to dispossess the petitioner from the land admeasuring Ac.0.03 cents in Sy.No.66/8B of Vepagunta Village, Puttur Mandal, Tirupati District, without following the procedure contemplated under Act 30 of 2013, Pending disposal of WP 33793 of 2025, on the file of the High Court.

The petition coming on for hearing, upon perusing the Petition and the affidavit filed in support thereof and upon hearing the arguments of SRI V VINOD K REDDY, Advocate for the Petitioner, Additional Solicitor General of India for Respondent No.1, learned GP FOR REVENUE for the Respondent Nos.2 to 5, the Court made the following ORDER:
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader for the respondents.

On perusal of the documents filed along with the writ petition, Ex.P5 discloses that the respondent authorities are proposing to release the amount for an extent of Ac.0.03 cents in favour of the 6th respondent.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that, in the year 2011, the respondent authorities issued a notification for acquiring land admeasuring Ac.0.11 cents, and initially,
compensation was paid to the petitioner's brother for an extent of Ac.0.08 cents.
However, no compensation was paid for the remaining Ac.0.03 cents.
It is submitted that the petitioner continues to remain in possession of Ac.0.03 cents, and the authorities have not taken possession of the said extent.
Therefore, the petitioner had no occasion to raise any objection earlier with regard to Ac.0.03 cents.
In these circumstances, the respondents are now contemplating to release the amount in favour of the 6th respondent and proceed with the acquisition of the remaining Ac.0.03 cents as well.
Considering the submissions, the respondents are directed not to release the amount.

The learned counsel for the petitioner is permitted to take out personal notice to the 6^*'
respondent through RPAD and file proof of service before the Registry.
Post the matter after three (03) weeks.
